name: Kernex Microsystems (India) Ltd
tagline: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs504cr > all FY26; order book Rs3,487cr vs Rs2,914cr mcap; TCAS-led multi-year growth story; 268 debtor days remain elevated.
business_overview: Kernex Microsystems manufactures advanced electronic safety systems and software solutions for the Indian railways (TCAS - Train Collision Avoidance System) and exports to global defence/aerospace markets. 100% Export Oriented Unit with ISO 9001 certification. FY26 revenue was flat but Q1 FY27 marked a significant inflection with Rs504cr revenue (largest quarterly ever), driven by accelerating Kavach/TCAS order execution and receivables collection.
fundamentals_table: Rs 504 Cr (largest quarterly revenue ever; +98% YoY standalone)
Rs 3,487 Cr (1.2x annual revenue; primarily Kavach/TCAS orders)
268 days (elevated; typical of large-contract defence/railway business)
0.00% (no dividend paid; all profits retained for capex/growth)
technical_read: As of 01-Oct-2026, Kernex trades at Rs 1,644, having recovered strongly from its 52-week low of Rs 850 (93% upside from lows). The stock sits comfortably above its 30W and 50W EMAs, reflecting sustained technical strength through Q1 FY27's earnings inflection. P/E of 14.5x is materially below the sector median (~39.4x), suggesting valuation reset room if Kavach ramp proves durable. Volume profile and liquidity have improved with FII entry (2.48% Jun 2026 vs 0% a year ago) and broader institutional participation, signaling institutional confidence in the turnaround. 52-week trading range (Rs 850-2586) reflects the market repricing from years of losses to the Q1 FY27 earnings inflection.
verdict_headline: TCAS-led multi-year growth inflection now visible in Q1 FY27 numbers; order book de-risks revenue ramp; valuation reset room at 14.5x P/E if execution persists.

four_box.note: Tailwind: Indian railways modernization (Kavach/TCAS mandate) + global defence/aerospace demand are structural. TAM: Kavach alone represents Rs 1L+ Cr addressable market across 80k+ km of Indian railways. Moat: Proprietary TCAS/Kavach IP, first-mover advantage in India's signal modernization, decade-long OEM relationships with Indian Railways. Valuation: weak (14.5x P/E is cheap vs growth visible in FY26-27 execution ramp, but order book concentration risk on Indian Railways budget/political cycles remains; debtor days of 268 embed working-capital risk). Score 3.0 = yes/yes/yes/weak = solid franchise operating in a structural growth market.
